title: Trent, Session 6, canon 4
source_text: IV. Atque huc spectat Canon Concilii Tridentini qui est quartus Sessionis sextae. Si quis dixerit, Liberum hominis Arbitrium a Deo motum & excitatum nihil cooperari assentiendo Deo excitanti atque vocanti, quo ad obtinendam justificationis gratiam se disponat, ac praeparet, neque posse dissentire, si velit, sed velut inanime quoddam nihil omnino agere, mereque passive se habere: anathema sit.
pass_a_gloss: IV. And hither looks the Canon of the Council of Trent which is the fourth of the sixth Session. If anyone shall say that the free Choice of man moved and aroused by God in no way cooperates by assenting to God arousing and calling, whereby it disposes and prepares itself for obtaining the grace of justification, and that it cannot dissent, if it will, but like something inanimate does nothing at all, and behaves merely passively: let him be anathema.
pass_b_english: Trent's sixth session, in its fourth canon, has the same aim. It runs: 'If anyone says that man's free choice, moved and roused by God, cooperates not at all by assenting to God who rouses and calls, whereby it disposes and prepares itself to obtain the grace of justification; that it cannot dissent if it wishes; but that like some lifeless thing it does nothing whatever and is merely passive: let him be anathema.'
